title: 15-Minute Honey Soy Glazed Salmon (My Lazy Tuesday Skillet Savior)
description: Crispy, sticky honey soy glazed salmon made in one skillet in 15 minutes. Perfect for crazy weeknights when you're too exhausted for takeout dishes.
story: It was 7:15 PM on a damp Tuesday, my inbox was still pinging, and my brain was completely fried. I opened a food delivery app, put a bowl of spicy noodles in my cart, and saw a $38 total with service fees and tip. Absolutely not. I slammed my laptop shut, dug through my tiny apartment fridge, and spotted two salmon fillets from Aldi. Ten minutes later, I had crisp-skinned fish sizzling in butter, honey, and soy sauce, smelling like absolute heaven. The first time I tested this last winter, I dumped the sauce in with the burner on high and practically turned the honey into smoky charcoal. Lesson learned: drop the heat before the sauce hits the pan. Now, this sticky, sweet-savory skillet dinner is my ultimate weapon against weeknight takeout regret.
ingredients: 2 center-cut salmon fillets (6 oz each, skin-on)
1 tbsp avocado oil (or any high-heat cooking oil)
1 tsp sriracha or chili crisp (optional, for gentle heat)
2 cloves garlic, finely grated on a microplane
1/4 tsp kosher salt and fresh cracked black pepper
instructions: Step 1: Pat the salmon completely dry with paper towels—moisture is the enemy of a crisp crust. Season both sides with kosher salt and cracked black pepper.

Step 2: Heat the avocado oil in a 10-inch stainless steel or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Place the fillets flesh-side down and sear undisturbed for 4 minutes until a deep golden crust forms.

Step 3: Carefully flip the fillets skin-side down. Immediately turn the heat down to medium-low. Drop in the Kerrygold butter, grated garlic, and ginger, letting them sizzle gently for 30 seconds until fragrant without scorching.

Step 4: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, and sriracha in a small ramekin, then pour it right around the salmon. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, tilting the skillet and spooning the bubbling glaze over the top until the sauce turns glossy and the salmon flakes easily with a fork.
proHack: Don't pour cold honey-soy sauce directly onto high heat. Turn the burner down to medium-low right after the flip and add the butter first; the milk solids in the butter emulsify with the honey and soy, keeping the glaze glossy instead of separating into burnt sugar.
storage: Store leftover fillets in an airtight glass container in the fridge for up to 2 days. To reheat without overcooking the fish into rubber, warm it in a skillet over low heat with a tiny splash of water and a lid on for 3 minutes, or flake it cold over leftover Trader Joe's jasmine rice.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the honey if I run out?
faqs.answer: Yes! Pure maple syrup works beautifully and adds a cozy woodsy note, or you can dissolve 1.5 tablespoons of dark brown sugar right into the soy sauce.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the honey glaze from burning in the skillet?
faqs.answer: The secret is killing the searing heat before the glaze touches the metal. Honey scorches fast, so turn the burner down to medium-low right after flipping your salmon, and keep spooning the sauce over the fish so it coats rather than sticks to dry spots.
